taxonomy.title: Hernia — ventral, incisional and abdominal wall
taxonomy.scopeIn: Umbilical/epigastric, incisional and Spigelian hernias, diastasis, fascial closure, mesh selection/plane and abdominal-wall reconstruction.
taxonomy.scopeOut: Groin hernia belongs to hernia-groin. Stoma-specific hernia care belongs to ostomy-enterocutaneous-fistula. General postoperative wound source control belongs to surgical-infection-antibiotics.
taxonomy.priorityReason: Mesh, contamination and reconstruction decisions extend a large existing recognition-focused bank.
taxonomy.coverageReason: Live identities cover part of this scope. The research agenda flags breadth to check, and the topic worker must judge redundancy and question quality.
taxonomy.testingWeightBasis: Owner-directed editorial estimate of general-surgery testing relevance. No exam percentages or official blueprint weights are asserted.

record.title: Mesh after a controlled enterotomy
fairness: One defensible best implant among these options: the learner must interpret the controlled contamination, viable repair and separable retromuscular plane, then apply material selection rather than reflexively choose biologic mesh. The observations are necessary eligibility information, not an answer-label match.

Importance: high-yield abdominal-wall practice and examination content. Realism: a single-stage intraoperative implant decision reviewed in clinic is credible; options name parallel, specific implants. The record does not imply that every enterotomy mandates immediate synthetic mesh.
No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. This is an offline editorial judgment, not verification of current comparative evidence or clinical approval.
suggestions: Retain the controlled contamination and tissue-plane details and have Melissa confirm the exact mesh-material ranking for the stated operative circumstances. No wording repair is required for editorial acceptance.

record.title: Mesh after a controlled enterotomy
fairness: One defensible best option among those offered: interpret controlled contamination and feasible retromuscular separation, then choose an appropriate mesh material. The small amount of suctioned fluid and closure observations are decision-critical rather than gratuitous reassurance. No exploitable grammar, length or convergence cue identified.

Importance: high-yield and practically consequential hernia-reconstruction judgment. Realism: suitable as retrospective hospital operative-record review, not an intervention performed in clinic. Implant choice remains clinician-dependent; this editorial PASS is not clinical approval or fresh evidence verification.
suggestions: Preserve the controlled-contamination and fascial-closure boundaries in any reuse; do not generalize this key to uncontrolled contamination or every implant position.

record.title: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan
fairness: The closure maneuver produces reversible respiratory/hemodynamic deterioration while bowel viability remains uncertain. Integrating those findings supports a staged abdominal strategy rather than immediate definitive reconstruction.

Temporary closure with planned re-exploration is the defensible best offered plan. The record does not establish a particular pressure threshold or assert that every dusky segment is irreversibly injured.

Importance: high for emergency general surgery and damage-control judgment. Realism: the described intraoperative decision is credible; the clinic frame is retrospective but does not confuse when the action occurs.

The combined/reassessment option is more cautious, but that is justified by two concrete operative observations rather than vague generic caution. The fascial-pressure maneuver is decision-critical evidence, not a gratuitous permission sentence.
suggestions: Retain the reversible closure response and unresolved viability as independent reasons that alter the operative plan.

Have the clinician verify exact temporary-closure/re-exploration indications and avoid feedback that treats observation of questionable bowel as permission to leave definitely nonviable bowel untreated.

record.title: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan
fairness: Two clinically consequential problems coexist: uncertain bowel recovery after release and reversible physiological intolerance of fascial approximation. The learner must integrate the need for reassessment with a safe closure strategy.

Temporary abdominal closure with planned re-exploration is a defensible best offered plan. The pattern does not require a formal abdominal-compartment diagnosis or an invented pressure threshold to show that the attempted closure is poorly tolerated.
Definitive component separation is a plausible reconstruction temptation, but does not resolve the uncertainty about bowel viability. The key is not simply the longest or only qualified answer.
Importance: high for emergency surgery, open-abdomen principles and bowel assessment. Realism: the historical operative decision is clearly distinguished from what the clinic delivers.
suggestions: Retain both the questionable bowel segment and reversible closure-related physiology. Clinical sign-off should keep temporary closure tied to the represented operative circumstances rather than implying it is routine for every emergency hernia.

record.title: Incisional hernia mesh selection
fairness: Report scope: the 11 new/revised executable drafts, each containing one decision node. Judgments use only each after Presentation, Exhibit, Task and Options; none has a separate Current update. Review-only key markers, explanations and author self-checks are not learner evidence. The four frozen prior PASS items are excluded. The 17 parked topics and one owner-held topic are noted but not graded; the disposition records are not additional executable questions. No network or fresh source verification was performed. Difficulty is a qualitative PGY-2/3 prediction. Editorial PASS is not clinical approval; all new versions remain needs_clinician_review pending Melissa Rowland's exact-version sign-off.

Node node.n4.ventral-controlled-enterotomy-mesh-material.v2: interpret the controlled bowel event together with the reconstructed pocket's relationship to bowel, then select an implant material. Mistaking this for direct visceral contact or treating any enterotomy as a reason to prefer biologic material produces distinct consequential errors. Moderate difficulty is credible.

Macroporous monofilament polypropylene is the defensible best of the offered materials for this expressly selected single-stage, closable, extraperitoneal reconstruction. The previously missing plane and closure information is now present. This judgment does not endorse single-stage repair for every enterotomy or claim that ePTFE is preferred in a contaminated intraperitoneal counterfactual.

No decisive nonmedical cue identified: the three options name concrete materials at comparable specificity, without a uniquely elaborate key, component convergence, diagnosis disclosure or a teaching sentence naming the polymer. The pocket description is necessary anatomical evidence.

Phase genuinely fits: source control and posterior-layer reconstruction have occurred, while the implant has not been selected. The current operative findings constrain the choice now. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified from the visible fields.
suggestions: Preserve the explicit selected-repair scope, primary-closure feasibility and separation of the prosthesis from bowel.
Keep the conclusion limited to this material comparison; do not extrapolate it into a universal timing or contamination rule. Obtain clinical sign-off on this exact version.

value.stem: Which closure plan best fits {patientName}'s findings at that point in the emergency operation?
value.explanation: Urgent transfer has already occurred; the decision is now whether to commit to definitive closure. Read the reversible pressure response at fixed ventilation together with bowel that still requires reassessment during resuscitation. Those findings support a temporary closure and planned re-exploration pathway, rather than applying a selected one-stage hernia repair rule to this different physiology. This new closure-stage teaching point requires targeted verification and surgical sign-off. No pressure threshold, re-exploration interval, mesh prohibition for every emergency repair or clinic-based operative capability is asserted.

answerChoices.label: Temporary abdominal closure with planned re-exploration
answerChoices.rationale: This preserves reassessment of uncertain bowel and avoids committing the represented patient to the physiologic effect reproduced by fascial approximation.

answerChoices.label: Primary fascial closure with permanent synthetic mesh reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: This is a definitive repair pathway, but selected controlled-contamination mesh rules do not settle uncertain viability or the represented intolerance of closure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is a definitive repair pathway, but selected controlled-contamination mesh rules do not settle uncertain viability or the represented intolerance of closure.

answerChoices.label: Component-separation reconstruction with definitive fascial closure
answerChoices.rationale: A larger definitive reconstruction does not address the immediate need to reassess bowel during ongoing resuscitation; the represented problem is not simply choosing a stronger elective closure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A larger definitive reconstruction does not address the immediate need to reassess bowel during ongoing resuscitation; the represented problem is not simply choosing a stronger elective closure.

value.displayName: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan
value.presentation: {patientName}, a 67-year-old woman, attends clinic after emergency surgery for an acutely painful irreducible incisional hernia with vomiting and guarding. The question concerns the end of that emergency exploration, after release of the constriction. One bowel segment remained dusky with patchy contraction while resuscitation continued. With ventilation settings and tidal volume unchanged, bringing the fascial edges together raised plateau pressure and lowered arterial pressure; releasing the edges reversed both changes. The operative team had not yet closed the abdomen.

value.learningSummary: Urgent transfer has already occurred; the decision is now whether to commit to definitive closure. Read the reversible pressure response at fixed ventilation together with bowel that still requires reassessment during resuscitation. Those findings support a temporary closure and planned re-exploration pathway, rather than applying a selected one-stage hernia repair rule to this different physiology. This new closure-stage teaching point requires targeted verification and surgical sign-off. No pressure threshold, re-exploration interval, mesh prohibition for every emergency repair or clinic-based operative capability is asserted.

value.patientPresentation: Oliver Hayes, a 10-year-old boy, visits the clinic with his father, Martin Hayes, who remains in the same room throughout the visit. Oliver has noticed a focal bump between the lower end of the breastbone and the navel. Standing makes it easier to see. Examination localizes a small upper-midline abdominal-wall defect with a fatty prominence. There is no navel or groin bulge and no acute pain or vomiting.

value.stem: Which hernia diagnosis best matches Oliver Hayes's upper-midline abdominal-wall finding?

answerChoices.label: Epigastric hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The focal defect lies in the upper abdominal midline and contains protruding fat, matching an epigastric hernia.

answerChoices.label: Umbilical hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel; this child's defect is above it.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel; this child's defect is above it.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An inguinal hernia is a groin finding, whereas this lump is in the upper abdominal midline.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An inguinal hernia is a groin finding, whereas this lump is in the upper abdominal midline.

answerChoices.label: Femoral canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: A femoral hernia is near the groin in the upper thigh, rather than above the navel.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A femoral hernia is near the groin in the upper thigh, rather than above the navel.

value.explanation: Oliver's focal fatty prominence arises through a defect in the upper abdominal midline, which fits an epigastric hernia. Localizing the defect distinguishes this finding from navel and groin hernias.
value.teachingPoint: Use the site of the focal defect to distinguish epigastric from umbilical and groin hernias.

value.stem: Which diagnosis best explains Ella Morgan's abdominal-wall lump?

answerChoices.label: Epigastric hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Uses the focal upper-midline fat-containing wall defect; the previous incision is at a different site.

answerChoices.label: Spigelian hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a lateral abdominal-wall defect near the semilunar line with the observed midline defect.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses a lateral abdominal-wall defect near the semilunar line with the observed midline defect.

answerChoices.label: Incisional hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Overweights the operative history without matching the current defect to the prior incision.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Overweights the operative history without matching the current defect to the prior incision.

answerChoices.label: Lumbar hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Confuses a posterior or flank wall defect with the anterior upper-midline finding.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Confuses a posterior or flank wall defect with the anterior upper-midline finding.

value.explanation: The focal upper-midline fat-containing defect supports epigastric hernia. Spigelian and lumbar defects occupy different abdominal-wall regions; an incisional hernia is related to an operative incision, which is elsewhere in this record. All offered diagnoses are abdominal-wall hernias.

Schedule repair immediately because the hernia is reducible

decisionNodes.explanation: Pulmonary fitness is a modifiable risk domain in elective incisional-hernia planning. value.patientPresentation: During elective ventral hernia repair, a small-bowel enterotomy is recognized and securely repaired. Contamination is minimal and controlled, there is no ongoing gross spillage, and the stable patient remains appropriate for single-stage repair.
value.stem: Which mesh should be selected?

answerChoices.label: Permanent macroporous monofilament synthetic mesh
Biologic mesh solely because an enterotomy occurred
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A controlled enterotomy does not by itself make biologic mesh the preferred material.

answerChoices.label: Permanent microporous multifilament synthetic mesh in the controlled field
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The approved material profile is macroporous and monofilament rather than microporous and multifilament.

answerChoices.label: Rapidly absorbable mesh as the routine choice for every contaminated field
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Clean-contaminated status does not make rapidly absorbable mesh the routine default for the selected repair.

value.patientPresentation: A stable patient is proceeding with single-stage incisional hernia repair after a recognized enterotomy was securely repaired with source control and no gross enteric spillage. The team is comparing mesh construction.

value.patientPresentation: The hospital hernia team is reviewing operative cases in which a bowel injury or contamination was encountered during ventral or incisional hernia repair.
value.stem: Which patient most clearly fits the approved macroporous-synthetic-mesh selection rule?

answerChoices.label: Uncertain bowel viability with incomplete source control and persistent contamination

value.stem: Which finding most clearly takes the case outside the approved rule?

answerChoices.label: Persistent gross enteric spillage despite attempted source control

answerChoices.label: Minimal contamination controlled intraoperatively

answerChoices.label: Stable physiology after the recognized bowel injury is securely repaired and controlled

value.stem: Which abdominal-wall reconstruction plan should be used for {patientName}?

exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Completed layer
items.value: The layer behind the rectus muscles has been approximated, separating the prepared mesh space from the abdominal contents.

items.label: Anterior view
items.value: The medial anterior fascial edges remain apart. With the temporary retractor released, gentle manual approximation brings the edges together at the midline.

items.label: Mesh space
items.value: The pocket lies behind the rectus muscles and in front of the newly closed posterior layer.

answerChoices.label: Primary fascial closure with mesh reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: Closing the posterior layer does not close the anterior fascial defect. The observed anterior edges are within the guideline's closable-defect scope.

answerChoices.label: Bridge the fascial defect with mesh reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: Leaving the readily closable anterior defect open is routine bridging, not the supported closure-and-reinforcement plan for this case.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Leaving the readily closable anterior defect open is routine bridging, not the supported closure-and-reinforcement plan for this case.

answerChoices.label: Component separation before mesh reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: The present edges meet without a release, so adding an advanced release is not required to solve the displayed closure problem.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The present edges meet without a release, so adding an advanced release is not required to solve the displayed closure problem.

value.explanation: There are two different layers in this record. The closed posterior layer separates mesh from the abdominal contents; it does not close the anterior fascial defect. For the displayed readily closable midline defect, approximate anterior fascia and reinforce it with mesh. The recommendation does not require forceful closure or an unnecessary advanced release.

value.patientPresentation: Ella Morgan, a 6-year-old girl, visits the clinic with her mother, Rachel Morgan, who remains in the same room throughout the visit. Her mother points out a small focal lump in Ella's upper abdominal midline, above the navel. Examination identifies a small abdominal-wall gap with protruding fat at that site. The navel and groins have no bulge. Ella is comfortable and has no vomiting.

value.stem: Which diagnosis best explains Ella Morgan's focal upper-midline abdominal-wall defect?

answerChoices.label: Epigastric hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The focal defect lies in the upper abdominal midline and contains protruding fat, matching an epigastric hernia.

answerChoices.label: Umbilical hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel; this child's defect is above it.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel; this child's defect is above it.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An inguinal hernia is a groin finding, whereas this lump is in the upper abdominal midline.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An inguinal hernia is a groin finding, whereas this lump is in the upper abdominal midline.

answerChoices.label: Femoral canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: A femoral hernia is near the groin in the upper thigh, rather than above the navel.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A femoral hernia is near the groin in the upper thigh, rather than above the navel.

value.explanation: Ella's upper-midline defect with protruding fat supports an epigastric hernia. An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel, and inguinal and femoral hernias occur near the groin.
value.teachingPoint: A focal fat-containing abdominal-wall defect above the navel supports epigastric hernia.

The navel and groins have no bulge. Ella is comfortable and has no vomiting.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnosis best explains Ella Morgan's focal upper-midline abdominal-wall defect?

answerChoices.label: Epigastric hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The focal defect lies in the upper abdominal midline and contains protruding fat, matching an epigastric hernia.

answerChoices.label: Umbilical hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An umbilical hernia is centered at the navel; this child's defect is above it.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An inguinal hernia is a groin finding, whereas this lump is in the upper abdominal midline.

answerChoices.label: Femoral canal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: A femoral hernia is near the groin in the upper thigh, rather than above the navel.

question.explanation: A collapsed fluid cavity is not the same as eradication of implant infection. The documented drainage and culture-directed course were adequate, yet purulence and the same organism recurred at the retained mesh. clinicalCase.presentation: Daniel Brooks, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic while the founder reviews his hospital records after his first incisional mesh repair. Drainage had begun recently. At the recorded assessment he was alert, eating and haemodynamically stable. The operative record placed macroporous monofilament polypropylene outside the peritoneal cavity. CT showed a localized fluid cavity around part of that mesh. A deep sample grew bacteria; the skin opening communicated with the cavity. No bowel communication was demonstrated on the completed evaluation.

independentReview.title: Daniel Brooks: recurrent infection after drainage and antibiotics
fairness: A collapsed collection conflicts with recurrent purulence and the same deep organism. The learner must recognize persistent implant infection despite radiographic drainage success, then escalate source control.

Mesh excision/debridement is the best offered recommendation. Superficial sinus removal does not address the documented deep focus, and repeating drainage is poorly supported when the cavity has collapsed.
The explanation appropriately leaves removal extent and reconstruction to the treating team; it should not be read as mandating complete explantation for every infection.

The sequence follows initial salvage coherently. The update repeats the intervention, microbiology and outcome needed for later entry; previous feedback does not pre-answer this failure decision. No confident clinical inaccuracy was identified offline.
suggestions: Retain imaging improvement alongside microbiological/clinical recurrence; removing either weakens the inference. Clinical approval remains separate.

fairness: She asks for repair before pregnancy, so the answer does not merely mirror her preference. The learner must account for pregnancy's effect on repair durability and balance that against a tolerable reducible hernia.
Pre-pregnancy mesh and suture repair are credible competing preventive strategies. Deferral is the best offered timing recommendation in this low-burden setting.
The standalone chronology and task are clear. The explanation preserves reassessment if symptoms change and avoids a universal material rule. No confident clinical inaccuracy was identified offline.
suggestions: Retain the contrast between the requested pre-pregnancy operation and tolerable symptoms. Clinical approval remains separate.

answerChoices.label: Start core rehabilitation; observe the focal navel defect at follow-up

question.explanation: There are two findings: a broad intact but separated midline and a focal reducible opening. The weakness follows the broad segment, not the focal protrusion. Consider rehabilitation first and observe the asymptomatic focal defect. If symptoms instead localized to that opening and improved with reduction, the focal repair pathway would become more appropriate.

clinicalCase.presentation: Maya Bennett, a 47-year-old woman, attends clinic because her middle abdomen domes and feels weak when she rises from a chair. Ultrasound during the movement shows the rectus muscles separating across a broad segment while tissue remains continuous between them. A separate small opening at the navel admits fat during straining and empties when she lies down. Pressing the navel and reducing that protrusion do not reproduce or relieve the weakness; supporting the broad midline does. She has not tried supervised rehabilitation.

independentReview.title: Maya Bennett: observation of a minimally symptomatic primary hernia

cues.phrase: She prefers to avoid an operation if observation is reasonable.
cues.why: The only nonoperative option directly fulfills the stated preference. Combined with the painless, activity-preserving course, this largely supplies the answer.

cues.phrase: Observe with scheduled reassessment and return precautions
cues.why: Only the key is furnished with reassuring follow-up and safety language; the competitors are simply operations.

fairness: Observation is a defensible best answer. The issue is difficulty, not a confident clinical inaccuracy: immediate exploration has no credible indication, leaving a preference-matching exercise.
Sequence: the first explanation says repair remains an option if the balance changes. This scaffolds the later work-interruption node.

Review-wide scope: all 23 candidate executable nodes were assessed from presentation, update, task, options and explanation; no separate exhibits are present. Eleven Keep records, 31 Retire-and-replace records and five held/parked teaching points were noted but not adjudicated; candidate replacements are included. No network or source re-verification was performed. PASS means editorial acceptance, not clinical approval; drafts require Melissa Rowland's exact-version clinical sign-off. Difficulty and high-yield judgments are qualitative, not measured exam frequencies.
suggestions: Keep necessary symptom, reducibility and preference information. Introduce a genuinely competing clinical consideration whose interpretation changes whether observation is appropriate, with credible current dispositions.
If retained as simple observation counseling, seek an explicit foundational-purpose exception rather than label it a difficult two-step resident item.
Give options comparable follow-up scope and remove the unsupported emergency-operation foil.

authorGate.coverTheKey: All options are hospital source-control procedures, two retain mesh and one removes it. Resuscitation/antibiotics are shared context, not unique key components. Removed outpatient delay and a uniquely cautious assessment key.
authorGate.sameDecisionStageAndCategory: Hospital source-control procedure after common initial resuscitation and antimicrobial treatment, reviewed later in clinic.
twoConsequentialSteps: Locate the infected focus using the cavity, drain and specimen provenance rather than equating the skin opening with superficial disease.
Use the documented systemic deterioration to choose operative mesh-source control over a drainage-and-retention attempt.
authorGate.residentDifficultyPrediction: Predicted moderate. Requires source-depth interpretation and recognition of the limitation of salvage; no high-confidence individualized superiority estimate is claimed.

oneBestAnswer.decidingObservation: A drain-confirmed periprosthetic purulent focus with matching blood culture accompanies confusion and hypotension after initial resuscitation had begun.
oneBestAnswer.closestError: Choose percutaneous salvage because a cavity is visible, overlooking the systemic course and sampled deep source.
oneBestAnswer.counterfactual: With stable localized disease and no systemic deterioration, monitored drainage/retention becomes reasonable. If the same systemic illness instead arose from another documented source and this wound were superficial, mesh excision would not follow merely from the skin opening.

authorGate.deletionTest: Deleting the deep compartment evidence makes mesh excision an unsupported target even though urgent hospital treatment remains needed. Deleting the systemic deterioration makes salvage a credible alternative. The already-started common care removes the old emergency-versus-outpatient cue.
authorGate.visibleSequenceAudit: Standalone round-2 candidate. No scored companion or earlier feedback is visible; all necessary history is supplied here.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: One attempt changes the choice stage from urgent disposition to the actual source-control target. Retains the source-control concept identity. SAGES guideline 31 was rechecked; independent cohort supports depth/selection without proving patient-level causality.

distractorAudit.temptation: Extends a real stable-patient salvage strategy to a septic prosthetic focus.
distractorAudit.whyNotHere: Drainage can support selected stable salvage, but a drain already reaches this cavity and the patient has developed systemic deterioration from the documented deep focus.
distractorAudit.correctUnder: A stable localized early infection, with no systemic organ-perfusion deterioration and a drainable collection, can support monitored specialist salvage.

distractorAudit.temptation: Treats the surface opening as the whole source.
distractorAudit.whyNotHere: Debriding the accessible skin opening would leave the documented prosthetic-plane source in place. Its visibility does not define the infection depth.
distractorAudit.correctUnder: If clinical and imaging evidence confined infection to skin/subcutaneous tissue and the prosthetic plane was uninvolved, wound-directed debridement with retention could be appropriate.

constructedObservations: Named patients, chronology, measurements, acquisition logs and suture accounting are constructed data, not empirical thresholds or test-performance claims.

question.stem: Which planning pathway best fits Grace Allen's present optimization course, remaining risk and changing hernia burden?

answerChoices.label: Begin hernia-team risk and repair planning at her current weight
answerChoices.rationale: This opens a concrete individualized risk/benefit and repair assessment while weight measures continue. It does not schedule an operation without informed choice. Progressive symptoms after a genuine unsuccessful weight-loss effort make indefinite exclusion potentially harmful.

answerChoices.label: Complete another supervised weight-loss course before hernia-team planning
answerChoices.rationale: Further weight management remains useful, but making another unsuccessful cycle a condition for any repair planning discounts progressive symptoms and enlargement.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Further weight management remains useful, but making another unsuccessful cycle a condition for any repair planning discounts progressive symptoms and enlargement.

answerChoices.label: Complete a bariatric-surgery assessment before hernia-team repair planning

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A bariatric discussion may be reasonable, but the supplied evidence does not require it before hernia-team assessment in this symptomatic, technically repairable case.

question.explanation: Interpret both trajectories: an actual weight-management effort has not changed the remaining risk, while symptoms and defect burden have worsened. Begin hernia-team planning now, with continued optimization and a specific risk-benefit discussion. This decision allows assessment; it neither guarantees a favorable operative balance nor schedules surgery before Grace chooses.

clinicalCase.presentation: Grace Allen, a 63-year-old woman, attends clinic about her incisional bulge. Her current BMI is 37. She completed the agreed supervised weight-management programme and continues its measures, but her weight has remained at the same level. Her respiratory symptoms have returned to baseline after treatment, she no longer smokes, and her treating team considers diabetes controlled. Meanwhile the bulge has enlarged and reduction-responsive pain repeatedly stops ordinary household tasks. It still reduces and she has no vomiting or persistent tenderness. The hernia surgeon considers repair technically possible; Grace has not yet chosen whether to proceed.

question.stem: Which plan should now guide Grace Allen's hernia care after pre-optimization?

answerChoices.label: Proceed with elective hernia repair scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: After a dedicated unsuccessful weight-loss effort, worsening function and enlargement can shift the balance toward repair planning.

answerChoices.label: Defer elective hernia repair for further weight loss
answerChoices.rationale: Further delay has real symptom and defect costs; there is no supported universal target supplied that must be reached first.

question.explanation: Optimization is not a rule to delay every symptomatic repair indefinitely. Grace completed a genuine effort, other risks improved, and the hernia is enlarging with worsening function. Those observations support a new repair discussion while preserving explicit counseling about the remaining weight-associated risks.

She also has COPD; she now becomes breathless walking across the room and uses her rescue inhaler more often than before. Her examination shows diffuse expiratory wheezing rather than focal hernia tenderness.

decisionNodes.stem: Which step should guide Grace Allen's elective hernia scheduling now?

answerChoices.label: Arrange respiratory reassessment before elective scheduling
answerChoices.rationale: The symptomatic hernia merits planning, but the current respiratory deterioration is a modifiable elective risk that needs assessment.

answerChoices.label: Arrange elective scheduling using current respiratory treatment
answerChoices.rationale: The new breathlessness, escalating rescue use and wheeze need reassessment before final elective scheduling.

answerChoices.label: Transfer for emergency hernia exploration during this visit
answerChoices.rationale: The hernia itself reduces and has no acute obstructive or persistent local findings; respiratory assessment is a separate need.

independentReview.title: Grace Allen: further weight loss versus symptomatic delay
clarityIssues: Neither presentation nor update describes her current degree of excess weight or remaining risk burden despite centering the decision on weight-associated operative risk.
Wants to reconsider surgery after discussing the risks is not the same as choosing surgery after informed counseling.

cues.phrase: She completed a supervised weight-loss programme without sustained weight reduction.
cues.why: Both distractors demand more weight-driven delay; this plus worsening symptoms strongly signals the sole proceed option. Keep this necessary history and improve the competing plans instead.

fairness: Balancing unsuccessful optimization and worsening function against operative risk is a meaningful two-step decision.
The explanation supports a new repair discussion, but the key commits to scheduling. The stated preference and risk assessment do not establish that scheduling has been chosen.

One unsuccessful programme alone does not resolve further optimization versus repair. Missing obesity/risk context leaves uncertainty; no universal BMI cutoff or obligatory bariatric-first rule should be invented.
Respiratory improvement is coherently updated and understandable without remembering the earlier answer.
suggestions: Align task, key and explanation at the same stage: compare concrete reevaluation/planning pathways or establish that risk-benefit assessment and patient choice have occurred.
Provide supported current weight/risk context sufficient to interpret the tradeoff without an invented threshold.
Replace automatic bariatric-first deferral with a genuinely plausible alternative for this patient if supported.

authorGate.coverTheKey: Removed the ambiguous non-escalating support shorthand. Necessary negative findings are retained because they distinguish temporary from definitive cavity coverage. All options are concrete closure strategies; no option is marked as simple or unnecessarily complex in its label.
authorGate.sameDecisionStageAndCategory: End-of-operation closure after emergency source control, reviewed later in clinic.
twoConsequentialSteps: Interpret the end-of-case findings as source control and physiological recovery without a bowel-reassessment indication, despite an unclosable fascial wall.
Select safe cavity coverage with deferred definitive reconstruction rather than immediate release or unnecessary planned open management.
authorGate.residentDifficultyPrediction: Predicted moderate, with narrow testing relevance. Difficulty comes from separating cavity coverage, reconstruction and a second-look indication, not from missing physiological information.

oneBestAnswer.decidingObservation: The bowel is in continuity, no further reassessment is planned, resuscitation derangement has resolved and tension-free sac/skin coverage is demonstrably feasible.
oneBestAnswer.closestError: Use temporary open-abdomen management merely because the fascial edges remain apart.
oneBestAnswer.counterfactual: If a remaining dusky segment required a planned second look, or circulation/ventilation worsened when coverage was tried, temporary coverage with re-exploration would become appropriate. If direct fascial closure were readily possible, this unclosable-defect branch would no longer apply.

authorGate.deletionTest: Each recovery/continuity/reassessment observation closes a formerly unresolved boundary. Removing safe coverage makes the key technically unsupported; removing the persistent gap removes the need to defer fascial reconstruction.
authorGate.visibleSequenceAudit: Standalone round-2 candidate. No earlier scored node or feedback is required; the complete relevant course is in this case.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: One attempt supplies actual physiology, continuity and re-exploration plan. EHS 2026 KQ4/4a and the stable/source-controlled scope were reverified on the public CC BY publisher page when PMC returned a challenge. No support cutoff is invented.

distractorAudit.temptation: Treats a fascial gap as a requirement for immediate definitive restoration.
distractorAudit.whyNotHere: The fascia does not meet directly in this emergency source-control operation. Current emergency guidance suggests deferring the added complex reconstruction rather than importing elective reconstruction goals.
distractorAudit.correctUnder: Later optimized elective reconstruction by a suitably experienced team can appropriately use a release if needed; width does not mandate a named release.

distractorAudit.temptation: Equates inability to close fascia with an obligatory second look.
distractorAudit.whyNotHere: The record now addresses the former uncertainties: bowel continuity/viability, no planned reassessment, resolved resuscitation need and safe available covering. The fascial gap alone is not a stated open-abdomen indication.
distractorAudit.correctUnder: Uncertain bowel viability requiring reassessment, continuing resuscitation, residual contamination or organ compromise during attempted coverage would favor temporary open management.

constructedObservations: Named patients, chronology, measurements, acquisition logs and suture accounting are constructed data, not empirical thresholds or test-performance claims.

question.stem: Which end-of-operation closure strategy best fits Martin Cole's recorded source-control, bowel and physiological findings?

answerChoices.label: Close with sac and skin; defer fascial reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: The source-controlled, recovered physiological state and available tension-free cavity covering permit cavity closure while complex definitive wall reconstruction is deferred. This follows a very-low-certainty conditional emergency recommendation.

answerChoices.label: Perform a myofascial release and definitive mesh reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: The fascia does not meet directly in this emergency source-control operation. Current emergency guidance suggests deferring the added complex reconstruction rather than importing elective reconstruction goals.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The fascia does not meet directly in this emergency source-control operation. Current emergency guidance suggests deferring the added complex reconstruction rather than importing elective reconstruction goals.

answerChoices.label: Apply temporary abdominal coverage and plan re-exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The record now addresses the former uncertainties: bowel continuity/viability, no planned reassessment, resolved resuscitation need and safe available covering. The fascial gap alone is not a stated open-abdomen indication.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record now addresses the former uncertainties: bowel continuity/viability, no planned reassessment, resolved resuscitation need and safe available covering. The fascial gap alone is not a stated open-abdomen indication.

question.explanation: First distinguish an unclosable fascial wall from an unresolved bowel or physiological problem. Here source control, continuity, recovery and feasible cavity coverage are documented. Close the cavity with the available sac and skin and defer complex reconstruction. This narrow 2026 recommendation is conditional and very low certainty; it is not a universal board rule for every emergency abdomen.

clinicalCase.presentation: Martin Cole, a 68-year-old man, attends clinic after discharge while the founder reviews his emergency incisional-hernia operation. The trapped damaged bowel was resected and continuity restored by an anastomosis. At final inspection the remaining bowel was perfused and contracting and no leak or undrained contamination was found. Vasopressors had been discontinued, perfusion and urine output had recovered, and the earlier acidosis had resolved. The operative and anaesthetic records documented no remaining resuscitation requirement or planned bowel reassessment. Gentle approximation still left a wide fascial gap. The sac and skin could meet over the contents without tension or a change in ventilation or circulation.

suggestions: Identify the bowel injury and baseline/end-of-case physiological status, with relevant source-control observations and no invented numerical cutoff.
Have the clinician confirm this exact spill/injury scenario is within the recommendation ranking permanent synthetic versus biologic material.

This is a separate one-node case. Painless presentation followed by a later painful update is coherent, but it cannot rely on the observation decision in the other Erin Walsh case.

question.stem: Which response to the suture-length warning is supported by Peter Shaw's completed primary-closure record?

answerChoices.label: Retain the primary suture line without corrective resuturing
answerChoices.rationale: Used length is 72 minus 18 = 54 cm across the complete 12-cm closure, a 4.5:1 ratio. The observed bite/tension pattern is also appropriate, so the warning does not establish a primary-line defect. This does not decide prophylactic augmentation for every patient.

answerChoices.label: Replace the primary suture line using additional suture
answerChoices.rationale: The worksheet used unused length as consumed length. An actual 1.5:1 final consumption would justify concern, but that is not this completed-span record.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The worksheet used unused length as consumed length. An actual 1.5:1 final consumption would justify concern, but that is not this completed-span record.

answerChoices.label: Retain the primary suture line with onlay mesh augmentation
answerChoices.rationale: Onlay augmentation is a separate preventive choice in selected elective cases; it does not correct this erroneous consumption warning and is not indicated by the accounting result itself.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Onlay augmentation is a separate preventive choice in selected elective cases; it does not correct this erroneous consumption warning and is not indicated by the accounting result itself.

question.explanation: The numerator is consumed suture, not unused remnants: (72 minus 18)/12 = 4.5. The completed-span ratio exceeds the guideline technique value of at least 4:1, and the bite/tension observations support retaining the line. Correct the worksheet rather than redo an apparently suitable primary closure. This arithmetic neither guarantees healing nor answers a separate prophylactic-mesh indication.

clinicalCase.presentation: Peter Shaw, a 59-year-old man, attends clinic while the founder reviews a completed elective midline-laparotomy closure. The entire 12-cm aponeurotic incision was sutured continuously using a new 72-cm slowly absorbable suture. All unused remnants, including discarded tails, totalled 18 cm. The operative check described closely spaced short bites confined to aponeurosis, even edge apposition and no edge blanching or forceful traction. A transfer worksheet had placed 18 cm in the box labelled suture consumed and flagged the primary closure as under-sutured.

independentReview.title: Peter Shaw: revising an inadequate elective midline closure
clarityIssues: The surgeon paused before completing the closure makes 18 cm of suture over a 12-cm wound ambiguous: does 12 cm mean the length already closed or the full wound? A final ratio cannot be inferred from incomplete consumption over an unspecified completed span.

cues.phrase: wide, widely spaced bites incorporating muscle
cues.why: Stacks familiar suboptimal technique features before the only corrective option. The numerical record is unnecessary to select the intended answer.

cues.phrase: Replace the closure with a small-bites suture line
cues.why: Only this option repairs the advertised defect; both competitors retain it. Majority-word convergence does not assemble the key, but the choices remain a repair-versus-ignore shortcut.

fairness: 18/12 = 1.5 is correct only if the lengths describe the same fully sutured span. The prose does not securely establish that denominator.
Small-bites aponeurotic closure and adequate suture-to-wound ratio are familiar elective principles; no confident clinical error is identified in the general principle stated.
Onlay mesh does not itself correct a poor suture line, but these alternatives require little beyond recognizing the advertised technique defect.
This is surgical technique with arithmetic, not a statistics-method item; the statistics single-skill exception does not automatically apply.
suggestions: Clarify that recorded consumption covers a specified fully approximated segment, or give a completed closure record.
Use a credible near-miss requiring interpretation to decide whether to redo or augment closure rather than stacking obvious defects.
Do not introduce new numerical technique rules without direct support.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should Maya Bennett follow for her current navel bulge?

cases.presentation: Daniel Brooks, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic while the founder reviews his hospital records after his first incisional mesh repair. Drainage had begun recently. answerChoices.rationale: Excision may become necessary, but the record does not yet show failed salvage or sepsis making this the preferred initial choice.

answerChoices.rationale: The cultured cavity lies at the implant plane; treating the exit does not control the deep focus.

decisionNodes.stem: Which closure plan best addresses Peter Shaw's recorded findings?

answerChoices.label: Replace the closure with a small-bites suture line

answerChoices.label: Retain the closure without mesh augmentation

answerChoices.label: Retain the closure and add onlay mesh augmentation

decisionNodes.explanation: The record shows sparse muscle-containing bites and a constructed suture-to-wound ratio of 18/12 = 1.5. definitions.name: Maya Bennett
definitions.presentation: Maya Bennett, a 47-year-old woman, attends clinic for a reducible navel bulge. It is painless and does not interrupt work or exercise. She prefers to avoid an operation if observation is reasonable. There is no vomiting or persistent tenderness.

nodes.objective: Choose an observation pathway when a primary hernia is reducible, asymptomatic and consistent with the patient's preference.
nodes.task: Which plan should Maya Bennett follow for her current navel bulge?

choices.label: Observe with scheduled reassessment and return precautions
choices.rationale: The current symptom burden and preference permit observation; reassessment preserves the option to repair if the burden changes.
choices.temptation: Balances operative morbidity against limited present impairment.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Arrange elective mesh repair at the next operative visit
choices.rationale: Elective repair is an option but scheduling it now overrides her expressed preference despite limited impairment.
choices.temptation: Treats every demonstrated defect as an operative indication.
choices.correctUnder: Persistent activity-limiting symptoms with a preference for repair would favor this pathway.

choices.label: Arrange hospital exploration during the current visit
choices.rationale: The bulge reduces and there are no acute obstructive or persistent local findings.
choices.temptation: Overweights the possibility of future incarceration.
choices.correctUnder: New nonreducibility with vomiting and focal guarding would require an urgent hospital pathway.

nodes.explanation: Interpret reducibility and symptom impact separately. Maya's present burden and preference support observation with review and clear acute return precautions. Repair remains an option if the balance changes.

steps: Distinguish a reducible, minimally disruptive defect from an acute complication.
Apply symptom impact and the stated preference to select observation rather than scheduling repair.
reasoning.closestError: Schedule surgery merely because a defect is present.
reasoning.decider: The bulge does not interrupt activity and Maya prefers observation.
reasoning.counterfactual: If pain repeatedly stopped work and Maya wanted repair, elective surgical planning would become preferable.
reasoning.deletion: Symptom impact and preference are both needed; removing either leaves elective repair more competitive. Reducibility and absent persistent symptoms set the safety boundary. No irrelevant medical history is supplied.
reasoning.cueAttack: All three options are concrete care pathways; removed a generic 'shared decision' key. The observation label has an explicit follow-up action, while both operative competitors are also complete plans. Complaint does not name a diagnosis.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate at the lower end; the error is automatic repair rather than ignorance of anatomy. No accepted-basic exception or measured difficulty claimed.
reasoning.sequence: First node. Feedback does not name a particular future symptom-triggered referral answer; later node receives a new functional trajectory.
reasoning.stage: Current disposition of a confirmed reducible primary hernia.
reasoning.repair: Replaces an abstract observation-and-repair counseling answer with an actual selected pathway and a preference that earns its role.

nodes.objective: Reassess a previously observed primary hernia when reduction-responsive pain starts preventing ordinary work.
nodes.task: Which plan should now replace Maya Bennett's observation pathway?
nodes.update: At follow-up, Maya stops lifting during each work shift because the focal navel bulge becomes painful. Lying down and reducing it stops the pain. It remains reducible, bowel function is unchanged, and she now wants definitive treatment.

choices.label: Refer for elective abdominal-wall repair planning
choices.rationale: New work interruption, local symptom concordance and changed preference alter the observation balance without establishing an emergency.
choices.temptation: Recognizes actual loss of function rather than the unchanged defect alone.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Continue observation at the previous review interval
choices.rationale: The previous minimally disruptive symptom pattern no longer applies.
choices.temptation: Anchors on the earlier observation decision because the defect still reduces.
choices.correctUnder: Stable tolerable symptoms and continued preference to avoid repair would support continued observation.

choices.label: Refer for emergency abdominal exploration today
choices.rationale: The local pain resolves with reduction and no current obstruction or persistent tenderness is described.
choices.temptation: Treats all increasing hernia pain as established strangulation.
choices.correctUnder: Pain persisting after loss of reducibility with vomiting or guarding would require urgent assessment.

nodes.explanation: The new evidence is failure of ordinary work because of pain that tracks the protrusion and resolves with reduction. That supports elective repair evaluation. Reducibility alone does not justify continuing the old plan, and the current findings do not establish an emergency.

steps: Attribute the new work interruption to a mechanically concordant focal protrusion.
Update the observation-versus-elective-repair decision while retaining the emergency boundary.
reasoning.closestError: Keep observing because the hernia still reduces.
reasoning.decider: Pain now stops actual shifts and resolves after reduction; the patient wants repair.
reasoning.counterfactual: If she performed full duties comfortably and still preferred observation, the previous observation option would fit.
reasoning.deletion: Removing the update removes the reason to change plans. Actual stopped tasks matter; merely performing modified work would be weaker evidence.
reasoning.cueAttack: Task asks for the changed plan without calling the hernia 'symptomatic enough for repair.' Options have similar length and each names a real disposition. No antibiotics or implausible organ referral fills the set.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate; distinguishes stable anatomy from changed functional indication and separates elective from urgent care.
reasoning.sequence: Earlier observation feedback does not say that work pain specifically mandates referral. A distinct interval change is necessary to reverse the earlier key.
reasoning.stage: Follow-up referral policy, not selection of a mesh polymer or operation technique.
reasoning.repair: Retains the stable referral concept; replaces an unexplained pain label with actual task failure and reduction response.

definitions.name: Luis Carter
definitions.presentation: Luis Carter, a 54-year-old man, returns to clinic after core rehabilitation for a broad midline ridge. His balance has improved, but lifting still produces focal pain above the navel. Standing examination shows fat protruding through a small gap there; pressure returning the fat through the gap stops the pain. The broad ridge itself is painless.

nodes.objective: Separate improvement of core symptoms from persistent pain attributable to a focal epigastric defect.
nodes.task: Which next plan best addresses Luis Carter's persistent lifting pain?

choices.label: Refer for elective epigastric hernia repair assessment
choices.rationale: The focal defect and reproducible reduction response identify a mechanical problem distinct from the improved core instability.
choices.temptation: Uses the current symptom response rather than the prior diastasis attribution.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Extend the same core rehabilitation programme
choices.rationale: Rehabilitation improved the broad functional complaint but has not addressed the focal reduction-responsive pain.
choices.temptation: Carries forward the earlier explanation for all midline symptoms.
choices.correctUnder: Diffuse core symptoms without a focal defect or local symptom concordance would support rehabilitation first.

choices.label: Observe the focal defect at routine annual review
choices.rationale: The specific ongoing task limitation warrants elective assessment rather than another incidental-defect review.
choices.temptation: Confuses a small reducible hernia with a clinically unimportant hernia.
choices.correctUnder: A painless incidental defect with no activity limitation could reasonably be observed.

nodes.explanation: Two problems can coexist. Improvement in balance does not explain away pain that is reproduced by protrusion through a focal defect and stops with reduction. That persistent mechanical symptom supports elective hernia assessment.

steps: Separate a focal defect from a broad intact widened midline and interpret the different treatment responses.
Refer for the remaining reduction-responsive mechanical symptom rather than repeat rehabilitation or passive review.
reasoning.closestError: Extend rehabilitation because some abdominal-wall symptoms improved.
reasoning.decider: Actual local protrusion and relief with reduction persist despite improvement in balance.
reasoning.counterfactual: Without a focal defect and reduction response, persistent diffuse core instability would favor further rehabilitation.
reasoning.deletion: The rehabilitation response and local reduction response each change causal attribution; removing the contrast weakens the indication being tested.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed 'confirmed symptomatic hernia requiring referral.' All options are specific ongoing care plans. The shortest option is a distractor; the key is not the only cautious comprehensive plan.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate from competing symptom attribution, not location recall.
reasoning.sequence: Standalone with the relevant prior response supplied. No earlier scored explanation reveals the current attribution.
reasoning.stage: Elective follow-up plan for the persistent symptom.
reasoning.repair: Keeps the original symptomatic-referral meaning and replaces a repeated diagnosis/referral chain with a consequential attribution problem.

definitions.name: Nora Ellis
definitions.presentation: Nora Ellis, a 62-year-old woman, attends clinic for a left-sided abdominal-wall lump that appears when she stands and strains. An outside ultrasound examined the marked site while she lay relaxed; no protrusion was seen. Standing examination reproduces tenderness beside the rectus, but the small lump disappears before its neck can be palpated.

nodes.objective: Recognize that a resting negative examination has not adequately tested an intermittent lateral abdominal-wall protrusion.
nodes.task: Which imaging plan best addresses the uncertainty in Nora Ellis's intermittent lateral lump?

choices.label: Targeted ultrasound during upright straining
choices.rationale: Reproduce the provoking conditions at the correct site to assess an intermittent defect missed at rest.
choices.temptation: Interprets acquisition conditions rather than treating 'negative ultrasound' as a final diagnosis.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Repeat targeted ultrasound while supine at rest
choices.rationale: Repeating the same acquisition does not address why the protrusion was missed.
choices.temptation: Assumes an additional scan is helpful without changing its conditions.
choices.correctUnder: A continuously palpable superficial lesion could be adequately assessed while resting.

choices.label: Routine supine CT without a provoking manoeuvre
choices.rationale: CT can diagnose this hernia, but repeating the resting condition is less directly suited to this small intermittent finding than targeted dynamic assessment.
choices.temptation: Escalates modality while leaving the provocation mismatch unchanged.
choices.correctUnder: A persistent deep mass, complex repair anatomy or obstructive symptoms would favor cross-sectional imaging.

nodes.explanation: The negative study sampled the correct site in a state when the lump disappears. Dynamic targeted assessment addresses that limitation. CT remains a valid diagnostic route in appropriate cases; this item does not declare ultrasound universally superior.

steps: Identify the mismatch between symptom provocation and the completed resting acquisition.
Choose a plan that changes that acquisition rather than accepting or merely repeating it.
reasoning.closestError: Order a second resting scan because the first result was negative.
reasoning.decider: The lump is present only while upright and straining, and the prior study used neither condition.
reasoning.counterfactual: If a fixed deep mass remained present at rest or a complex repair needed mapping, cross-sectional CT would become more useful.
reasoning.deletion: Without the acquisition log, repeated ultrasound versus CT cannot be ranked fairly. The examination is equivocal rather than a definitive palpable defect.
reasoning.cueAttack: All options are named imaging acquisitions and all receive wait metadata. 'Dynamic' is not supplied as a pre-answer interpretation; the learner must infer the acquisition problem. Key and rest competitor share the modality, avoiding an organ-name shortcut.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate at the lower end; CT is a credible competitor. Independent reviewer should specifically assess that acquisition-based ranking under the weak guideline.
reasoning.sequence: First node; feedback discusses test adequacy without naming the next repair recommendation.
reasoning.stage: Imaging acquisition for an unresolved intermittent wall finding.
reasoning.repair: Removes irrelevant organ ultrasound distractors; preserves recognition/workup identity because the previous variant already tested diagnostic clarification.

nodes.objective: Move a symptomatic anatomically confirmed Spigelian defect into elective repair assessment without assuming an emergency or a universal approach.
nodes.task: Which plan best addresses Nora Ellis's returned abdominal-wall findings?
nodes.update: The targeted study shows a focal opening beside the lateral rectus edge. A small sac enters between the abdominal-wall muscle layers during straining and returns when she relaxes. Pain at that site now prevents her walking to work; bowel function remains normal.

choices.label: Elective surgical assessment for mesh repair
choices.rationale: An interparietal lateral defect with meaningful symptoms warrants repair evaluation.
choices.temptation: Combines anatomy and symptom impact rather than requiring a large external mass.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Physiotherapy for widened midline connective tissue
choices.rationale: This is a focal lateral opening rather than an intact broad midline separation.
choices.temptation: Equates all abdominal-wall weakness with diastasis.
choices.correctUnder: Broad midline separation without a focal hernia would support physiotherapy first.

choices.label: Hospital admission for emergency exploration
choices.rationale: The observed sac returns and there are no current obstructive or ischemic findings.
choices.temptation: Treats a Spigelian location as sufficient evidence of current strangulation.
choices.correctUnder: New irreducibility, persistent pain and obstructive or peritoneal findings would require urgent assessment.

nodes.explanation: Infer a focal lateral interparietal hernia from the findings, then use its current symptoms and reducibility to choose the pathway. Elective mesh-repair assessment is appropriate. The evidence does not select one open or laparoscopic technique for every Spigelian hernia.

steps: Interpret the focal lateral interparietal protrusion rather than misclassify a broad midline process.
Combine substantial symptoms with reducibility to select elective repair evaluation.
reasoning.closestError: Treat a small intermittently visible defect with core therapy because it does not form a large external lump.
reasoning.decider: The study demonstrates a focal lateral opening and symptoms prevent an actual activity, but the sac returns.
reasoning.counterfactual: If only broad midline separation were present and no focal defect existed, physiotherapy would be reasonable; acute irreducibility would instead favor hospital assessment.
reasoning.deletion: The returned anatomy is required to distinguish core therapy from repair; the activity limitation distinguishes treatment from incidental observation. Normal bowel function and demonstrated return establish current phase.
reasoning.cueAttack: Neither complaint nor update uses the keyed diagnosis name. Every option names a concrete care pathway; no 'individualized technique' label. Referral is not inferred simply because an answer-specific word appears in the task.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate from localization, functional burden and urgency discrimination; requires independent assessment of the core-therapy distractor.
reasoning.sequence: First feedback addresses acquisition only. Returned anatomy and functional limitation are newly visible; prior knowledge of the planned ultrasound does not determine this plan.
reasoning.stage: Disposition after diagnostic results, not a choice between two unsupported operative techniques.
reasoning.repair: Retains elective-referral identity, adds an interparietal pattern and a genuine functional decision instead of generic management counseling.

definitions.name: Daniel Brooks
definitions.presentation: Daniel Brooks, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic while the founder reviews his hospital records after his first incisional mesh repair. Drainage had begun recently. At the recorded assessment he was alert, eating and haemodynamically stable. The operative record placed macroporous monofilament polypropylene outside the peritoneal cavity. CT showed a localized fluid cavity around part of that mesh. A deep sample grew bacteria; the skin opening communicated with the cavity. No bowel communication was demonstrated on the completed evaluation.

nodes.objective: Select an initial specialist-directed source-control attempt for a stable localized mesh infection without asserting that every infected implant requires immediate removal.
nodes.task: Which initial source-control plan best fits Daniel Brooks's recorded findings?

choices.label: Percutaneous drainage with culture-directed antibiotics
choices.rationale: This recently symptomatic stable localized extraperitoneal process can undergo a specialist-directed salvage attempt. The implant and course still require reassessment.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes treatment of a deep focus from immediate automatic explantation.
choices.correctUnder: Current case, with specialist supervision.

choices.label: Complete mesh excision with operative debridement
choices.rationale: Excision may become necessary, but the record does not yet show failed salvage or sepsis making this the preferred initial choice.
choices.temptation: Treats an infected prosthesis as categorically unsalvageable.
choices.correctUnder: Persistent infection after an adequate attempt or a septic course would support excision.

choices.label: Skin-tract debridement with local dressings
choices.rationale: The cultured cavity lies at the implant plane; treating the exit does not control the deep focus.
choices.temptation: Mistakes a small external opening for a superficial process.
choices.correctUnder: A superficial stitch focus with no deep communication could be managed locally.

nodes.explanation: A small skin opening can drain a deep prosthetic focus. Daniel's stability and localized findings permit a monitored salvage attempt using drainage and antibiotics, rather than surface care or automatic complete removal. The completed evaluation did not demonstrate a fistula; it does not guarantee one can never emerge.

steps: Use the tract and deep culture to localize infection at the prosthesis rather than the skin.
Use the stable localized course to choose an initial salvage attempt rather than immediate excision.
reasoning.closestError: Excise every infected mesh immediately, or under-treat it as a skin opening.
reasoning.decider: Documented deep infection is localized and the patient is stable before any adequate salvage attempt.
reasoning.counterfactual: If drainage and directed therapy failed with continuing deep infection, mesh excision would be more appropriate.
reasoning.deletion: Deep culture/communication establish the treatment target; stability and absence of a documented enteric connection establish the selected salvage scope. No material-specific success probability is inferred.
reasoning.cueAttack: All options are source-control procedures with similar specificity. The key is not labelled 'conservative' or 'individualized.' Negative bowel evaluation is necessary for the selected case, not proof of lifelong absence of fistula.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard; initial salvage versus definitive removal is a credible operative disagreement, so the low-certainty ranking needs Melissa's review.
reasoning.sequence: First node; feedback does not tell the learner what to do after a failed attempt. The next update must demonstrate actual failure.
reasoning.stage: Initial source-control strategy at the outside hospital, reviewed in clinic.
reasoning.repair: New concept explicitly versions a more specific strategy-selection meaning; old general referral history remains attached to its original identity.

nodes.objective: Escalate persistent deep mesh infection after a documented completed salvage attempt.
nodes.task: Which source-control recommendation now best fits Daniel Brooks's persistent infection?
nodes.update: The drain reached the cavity, the antibiotic course matched the deep culture, and repeat imaging showed that the fluid cavity had collapsed. Purulent drainage nevertheless returned through a tract to the retained mesh. Repeat deep culture grew the same organism. Daniel remained stable.

choices.label: Excise mesh and debride the repair plane
choices.rationale: Persistent microbiologically supported infection after adequate drainage and directed therapy raises a retained-prosthesis source-control problem.
choices.temptation: Interprets the actual completed attempt rather than the smaller residual cavity as success.
choices.correctUnder: Current case.

choices.label: Retain mesh and repeat drainage with directed antibiotics
choices.rationale: The cavity was already drained and the regimen matched the organism, yet infection recurred at the implant.
choices.temptation: Repeats a previously reasonable plan despite documented failure.
choices.correctUnder: An undrained residual collection or a previously mismatched antibiotic would justify correcting that failure before declaring salvage unsuccessful.

choices.label: Retain mesh and excise the cutaneous sinus tract
choices.rationale: Closing or removing the tract alone leaves the documented deep infected focus.
choices.temptation: Treats the visible outlet rather than the retained source.
choices.correctUnder: A superficial localized stitch sinus without implant-plane involvement could be excised locally.

nodes.explanation: A collapsed fluid cavity is not the same as eradication of implant infection. The documented drainage and culture-directed course were adequate, yet purulence and the same organism recurred at the retained mesh. Operative excision assessment is appropriate; the exact removal extent and reconstruction plan require the treating team.

steps: Recognize that adequate cavity drainage did not eradicate the implant-associated infection.
Escalate source control rather than repeat an already adequate identical attempt or close its outlet.
reasoning.closestError: Call the collapsed cavity a successful salvage despite recurrent purulence.
reasoning.decider: Actual adequate drainage plus matched therapy followed by recurrence with the same deep organism.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the first drain missed a persisting cavity, image-guided drainage correction would be reasonable before treating the prosthesis as failed salvage.
reasoning.deletion: Without documented drain adequacy and antibiotic matching, excision versus another salvage attempt is underdetermined. All update sentences establish that boundary.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed 'conservative management failed' from pre-answer context. Options name three source-control actions and keep rationales after answering. Neither the task nor the complaint announces explantation.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard from adequacy-versus-outcome interpretation; stable physiology is not evidence that persistent infection is harmless.
reasoning.sequence: The first node permits salvage; the update reverses its evidentiary basis and is necessary for the new key. No prior explanation says that every later sinus requires removal.
reasoning.stage: Source control after an actual completed attempt.
reasoning.repair: Retains specialist-source-control meaning and makes the missed inference concrete rather than asking for vague removal counseling.

definitions.name: Aisha Morgan
definitions.presentation: Aisha Morgan, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic after discharge. The founder reviews the earlier hospital assessment after ventral mesh repair. At that time her wound pain was increasing, she had become confused and hypotensive, and CT showed a fluid collection communicating with the prosthetic plane. Blood cultures and a deep aspirate grew the same organism.

nodes.objective: Recognize systemic deterioration from a deep prosthetic source as a hospital surgical source-control problem.
nodes.task: Which recommendation should have guided Aisha Morgan's care at that recorded assessment?

choices.label: Urgent operative source-control assessment with resuscitation
choices.rationale: The matched deep/blood organisms and deteriorating physiology require hospital source control, including mesh excision assessment.
choices.temptation: Connects the prosthetic focus with systemic deterioration.
choices.correctUnder: Current recorded phase.

choices.label: Outpatient drainage with a planned oral antibiotic course
choices.rationale: A stable outpatient salvage pathway does not fit confusion and hypotension.
choices.temptation: Extends a selected localized-infection pathway into a septic course.
choices.correctUnder: A stable localized infection without organ dysfunction may support monitored specialist salvage.

choices.label: Local wound debridement with routine clinic follow-up
choices.rationale: Local skin treatment does not address the bloodstream and prosthetic-plane focus.
choices.temptation: Underweights depth because the infection has a wound opening.
choices.correctUnder: A superficial wound focus without deep involvement or systemic illness could receive local treatment.

nodes.explanation: Interpret both the source and the physiology. This was a deep prosthetic infection with systemic deterioration, requiring hospital resuscitation and urgent surgical source-control assessment. It was not a stable outpatient salvage situation.

steps: Link the deep communicating collection and matching cultures to the systemic illness.
Choose urgent hospital source control rather than an otherwise reasonable stable salvage plan.
reasoning.closestError: Apply the stable mesh-salvage rule despite confusion and hypotension.
reasoning.decider: The record combines a verified deep focus with acute organ-perfusion deterioration.
reasoning.counterfactual: Stable localized disease without organ dysfunction could permit a specialist-directed drainage/antibiotic attempt.
reasoning.deletion: Depth and physiological change are both needed to distinguish local care from urgent source control. The clinic post-discharge frame prevents pretending the clinic has an ICU.
reasoning.cueAttack: No pre-answer sepsis label, no medication dose and no named missing referral. All options are actual source-control pathways. Residual safety recognition makes this the easiest draft; independent review must decide whether it is sufficiently demanding.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate at the lower end because the competing stable-salvage rule is clinically real; no accepted-basic status claimed.
reasoning.sequence: Standalone. Earlier stable-salvage feedback is not visible in this case.
reasoning.stage: Retrospective disposition at the outside hospital's deterioration point.
reasoning.repair: Retains the original source-control meaning; replaces vague fever/tachycardia wording with a verified deep focus and consequential physiology.

definitions.name: Helen Parker
definitions.presentation: Helen Parker, a 71-year-old woman, attends clinic after discharge while the founder reviews her referring hospital record. A previously intermittent lateral bulge became persistently painful and stopped reducing. At the recorded assessment the overlying area was tender with guarding. CT showed bowel trapped beside the rectus with reduced wall enhancement; she had passed stool earlier that day.

nodes.objective: Choose urgent operative evaluation when local and CT findings suggest ischemic hernia contents despite recent stool passage.
nodes.task: Which plan best fits Helen Parker's findings at that recorded assessment?

choices.label: Resuscitate and arrange emergency operative exploration
choices.rationale: Persistent nonreducibility, guarding and reduced enhancement raise concern for compromised bowel; recent stool passage does not negate those findings.
choices.temptation: Weights direct local/perfusion observations over a falsely reassuring bowel-history detail.
choices.correctUnder: Current recorded phase.

choices.label: Attempt repeated manual reduction and observe overnight
choices.rationale: Repeated reduction attempts are not the preferred path when ischemia is suspected.
choices.temptation: Treats all acutely stuck hernias as uncomplicated incarceration.
choices.correctUnder: A selected early incarcerated hernia without concerning local or perfusion findings could be considered for a supervised reduction pathway.

choices.label: Use nasogastric decompression and serial abdominal reviews
choices.rationale: Decompression does not resolve possible strangulation of trapped bowel.
choices.temptation: Applies an uncomplicated obstruction pathway because stool recently passed.
choices.correctUnder: A nonstrangulating obstruction without a trapped ischemic hernia focus could justify an initial nonoperative pathway under the relevant protocol.

nodes.explanation: The decisive evidence is the persistent trapped painful segment with guarding and reduced enhancement. Those findings outweigh recent stool passage and require urgent operative assessment. No lactate cutoff or complete-obstruction requirement is assumed.

steps: Interpret reduced bowel enhancement with persistent local findings as possible ischemia rather than simple intermittent incarceration.
Choose operative evaluation rather than reduction or decompression as the definitive pathway.
reasoning.closestError: Let recent stool passage justify a nonoperative obstruction plan.
reasoning.decider: Reduced enhancement and guarding at a persistently nonreducible defect.
